title: Config guardrail evaluation for batching + cache rollback policy
creator: Aisha Kumar
description:
Purpose: Build a deterministic, reproducible eval and monitoring harness that ties batching + prefix/KV cache configuration changes to both latency and quality signals and defines automated guardrails (canary thresholds and rollback policies).

Background: Recent internal tuning for continuous batching and prefix cache TTL produced measurable cost savings in internal benchmarks but raised sporadic quality regressions on focused slices (multiturn instructions and long-context summarization). We need a pre-deploy + continuous canary system that evaluates candidate configs along a latency-quality frontier and surfaces actionable thresholds for automated rollback.

Scope:
- Define a compact set of candidate config dimensions: microbatch_size, continuous_batch_window_ms, kv_cache_ttl_s, prefix_merge_enabled (bool), prefix_merge_threshold_tokens.
- Create a weighted eval suite (redwood-evals/batch-cache/2026-03) with slices: short-answers, long-context summarization (>=2048 tokens), multi-turn instruction-following, code-gen, and safety/ hallucination probes.
- Instrument per-request metrics: p95 latency (ms), tokenized length, model log-prob delta vs baseline, BLEU/ROUGE/F1 for applicable slices, hallucination-rate proxy (entity hallucination FPR), and a derived Quality-Per-Millisecond (QPM) metric defined as normalized quality_score / p95_latency.
- Design grid + adaptive search that first runs coarse grid (O(30) configs) then local Bayesian search in promising regions.
- Define canary rollout policy and auto-rollback rules to be consumed by the Console: baseline = current production config; success if median QPM >= baseline QPM * 0.995 AND slice-level hallucination_rate increase <= 0.5 percentage points.
- Produce dashboards, an automated regression alerting rule, and a PR template to attach evaluation artifacts for config/model changes.

Deliverables:
1) Eval harness code and CI job (redwood-ci/evals/batch_cache_guardrail) that emits per-config artifact (JSON + CSV) and an HTML summary.
2) New Console dashboard panels: config-compare latency/quality frontier, slice heatmap, automatic rollback recommendation.
3) Canary policy payload spec and an example rollout that the orchestration layer can apply.
4) Runbook with triage steps and known false-positive patterns.

Acceptance criteria:
- CI job runs in < 90 minutes for the coarse grid and produces deterministic artifacts.
- For a seeded regression (introduced by synthetic prefix_merge bug), the harness flags the config at or before 20% canary with an actionable alert and a recommended rollback.
- Dashboards show QPM curves and slice-differentiated signals.

Why this is different: Instead of only plotting latency-vs-quality frontiers, this ticket focuses on operationalizing a guardrail: a concrete metric (QPM), an automated canary rollback rule, and a lightweight search that is feasible to run in CI and in continuous monitoring. The aim is to reduce toil for on-call and accelerate safe config rollouts.

acceptance_criteria: 1) CI produces deterministic JSON artifacts for each config and a summary HTML; 2) QPM-based canary rule triggers on seeded regression during canary <= 20%; 3) Dashboard surfaces per-slice regressions and recommended rollback action; 4) Runbook validated in tabletop exercise.
notes: Potential false positives identified: traffic-induced tokenization differences and dataset drift. Mitigations: normalize on tokenized-length buckets and keep a small stable benchmark subset for calibration. Consider bounding tolerance tighter for safety-critical slices (safety & hallucination probes).
